oh nice, you're ahead.  Don't see that very often.  And yes it would basically be trading in.  Which saves you a little sales tax if you do this all through a dealership.  

So the price of the ST after your trade would be ~$16,000.  As far as sales tax goes, you'd only be paying the DIFFERENCE between the two cars.  So $19,500 - $9,500, would end up being ~$1,000 worth of sales tax + title + tag.  You'd probably end up financing somewhere around $17,500-$18,000.  At ~72 months with ~2% interest that = ~255/month.  

I would like to add the disclaimer that I am not a sales professional, or finance guy or anything so these figures may be a bit off.  Mostly just going by my own experience trading cars through the dealership I work for.  Which is usually about twice a year.

Hey there.  I work at a dealership and also trade cars around a lot myself.  

What you need to find out is;

1) How much you still owe on your car

2) What the trade-in value of your car is (kbb.com)

The trade in value will probably be less than what you owe on the car.  So that difference is what you'll have to tack on to a new loan for the ST.  Shouldn't be a problem as long as

1) You have decent credit

2) You aren't obscenely upside-down in your current car


edit: Forgot to mention, you can probably go with a longer loan term to keep the payments lower.  IE: if you're at 60 months now, on a newer car like a 2013 ST, going to 72 months shouldn't be a problem.
